column1: # Module 13 — shell + Bandit. Format: Text<TAB>tags. Card law: anki/CARD-RULES.md
What is the shell's sentence structure? {{c1::command --flags arguments}} — verb, adverbs, objects.
Where is the shell's dictionary? {{c1::man CMD}} · {{c2::CMD --help}} · {{c3::help BUILTIN}} — reading it beats guessing.
In the shell, what do pwd, cd -, and cd ~ do? {{c1::Where am I}} · {{c2::back to the previous directory}} · {{c3::home}}.
What does tail -f do, and when do you use it? {{c1::Follows a growing file live}} — the command you'll use most on real logs.
In shell paths, what are . / .. / ~ / - ? {{c1::Here}} · {{c2::parent}} · {{c3::home}} · {{c4::previous directory}}.
In shell globbing, what do * ? and ** match? {{c1::Any characters}} · {{c2::exactly one character}} · {{c3::any depth (modern shells)}}.
What does a shell pipe | do? {{c1::Sends one command's output into the next command's input}} — a conveyor of small machines.
In the shell, what does 2>&1 mean? {{c1::Send stderr (2) wherever stdout (1) currently goes}} — so pipes and logs capture errors too.
Why must sort come before uniq -c? {{c1::uniq only collapses ADJACENT duplicates}} — unsorted input silently gives wrong counts.
What does sort -rn do? {{c1::Sorts numerically (-n), reversed (-r) — biggest first}}.
Which question does find answer, and which does grep? find = {{c1::"which FILES?" (name/type/time/size)}} · grep = {{c2::"which LINES?" (content)}}.
What do grep's flags -r -n -i -l -c -v do? {{c1::Recursive}} · {{c2::line numbers}} · {{c3::case-insensitive}} · {{c4::filenames only}} · {{c5::counts}} · {{c6::invert the match}}.
What does xargs do? {{c1::Feeds a list of items into another command}}: find . -name '*.log' | xargs wc -l
Read the permission string -rw-r--r-- aloud. {{c1::Owner rw-, group r--, others r-- → only the owner can write}}.
What does chmod 600 secret.txt mean? {{c1::Owner read+write; group and others nothing}}.
Why does cat -oddly-named fail, and what are the two fixes? {{c1::It looks like flags}}; fix with {{c2::cat ./-oddly-named}} or {{c3::cat -- -oddly-named}}.
What is SSH, in one sentence? {{c1::An encrypted remote terminal — you type here, it runs there}} (ssh user@host -p PORT).
What is SSH's first-connect fingerprint prompt for? {{c1::The server proving its identity/continuity}} — be suspicious if {{c2::it ever changes unexpectedly}}.
What is the Bandit connection line? {{c1::ssh bandit0@bandit.labs.overthewire.org -p 2220}} (level-0 password: bandit0).
What is the house rule for Bandit? {{c1::No walkthroughs — 30 min struggle, then man pages, then concept-only hints}}; every walkthrough read is a rep not done.
Shell translation: bash's ls / cat / grep in PowerShell are {{c1::Get-ChildItem · Get-Content · Select-String}}.
Shell translation: bash reads an env var as $VAR; PowerShell reads it as {{c1::$env:VAR}}.
Shell translation: bash's /dev/null in PowerShell is {{c1::$null}}.
What does "labs are the curriculum" mean? {{c1::Cyber videos are on-ramps; hands-on labs (Bandit, PortSwigger, DVWA) are where competence forms}}.
